column1: # label_typo_review batch 2, 2026-08-04. Emma's ruling: MACRONS (Ōmi, Kōnomine).
# THE MACRON RULE AND THE MORPHEME RULE ARE THE SAME RULE, seen twice. A macron
# marks a LONG VOWEL. Two identical vowels that meet across a morpheme boundary
# are not one long vowel, they are two vowels — so 飯玉 いいたま is Iitama (batch 1)
# and 男乃宇刀 お・の・う・と is Onouto, while 神峯 こうのみね is Kōnomine because
# こう really is one long o.
# That distinction has a consequence worth stating plainly: for a dozen of these,
# THE LABEL WAS ALREADY RIGHT and the queue's own KANA_ROMANIZED column is the
# wrong side. It collapses every o+u it sees, so it reports Kotoura as "Kotora"
# and Horinouchi as "Horinochi" and then flags the correct label as divergent.
# Those are answered OTHER, not LABEL_TYPO — there is nothing to fix on Wikidata.
# Only cases where the label and the kana AGREE ON THE READING are answered here.
# Where they disagree about the reading itself (潮江 うしおえ vs Shioe, 豊栄 ほうえい
# vs Toyosaka, 敬満 きょうまん vs Keiman) the macron rule cannot settle it, and
# Emma's ruling on those is to research each — they stay pending.
# ─── LABEL_TYPO: long vowel, written the house way ───
# ─── LABEL_TYPO: the macron was in the wrong place, or a letter was lost ───
# ひのおうし is hi-no-ōshi, so the macron belongs on the third syllable, not the second.
# うじようだ is uji-yōda; the label had dropped the "iy" entirely.
# おおただねこ: long o at the front, and the label had "tata" for ただ.
# ─── OTHER: the LABEL is correct; KANA_ROMANIZED collapsed a morpheme boundary ───
